name: Question 5
problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}+6x{y}^{′}+6y=0,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}+6x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+6{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }+6\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+6{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)+6\lambda +6] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)+6\lambda +6 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}+5\lambda +6 & =0 \\ (\lambda +2)(\lambda +3) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the roots are $\lambda =-2$ and $\lambda =-3.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{-2}+{c}_{2}{x}^{-3}.
$$

Question 5
?

Find the general solution to the equation x2y″+6xy′+6y=0,x>0.

a
y(x)=c1x−1+c2x3
b
y(x)=c1x−2+c2x−3
c
y(x)=c1x−2+c2x−5
d
y(x)=c1x3+c2x4
e
y(x)=c1x2+c2x
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Note that the given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form y=xλ. Differentiating y with respect to x gives

y′=λxλ−1,y″=λ(λ−1)xλ−2.

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

x2⋅λ(λ−1)xλ−2+6x⋅λxλ−1+6xλ=0λ(λ−1)xλ+6λxλ+6xλ=0xλ[λ(λ−1)+6λ+6]=0.

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

λ(λ−1)+6λ+6=0λ2+5λ+6=0(λ+2)(λ+3)=0.

Hence, the roots are λ=−2 and λ=−3. Therefore, the general solution is y(x)=c1x−2+c2x−3.
